lesson_title: The Map Is Telling You a Story
hook_text: There is a thin blue line running beside a field on your map. It is worth two marks, and most people never notice it.
clip_script: Look at this map. A blue river. Next to it, a thin line running off the river and along the edge of some fields. That thin line is a furrow, a channel people dug to carry water. Put it together with the fields beside it and the map is telling you a story: irrigation farming. That is two marks, right there. Maps talk in symbols. Dots for things at one place, lines for long things, patches for areas. Blue is water, brown is the land, green is trees, red is main roads, black is buildings and writing. A solid blue river flows all year. A broken blue river only flows after rain, so you are in a dry area. Lots of windmills and hardly any fields? Cattle or sheep, water pumped from underground. A mine dump and a big hole? Mining. And the dam? People built the wall, so the dam is a constructed feature, not a natural one. Read the clues together.
visual_style: A map tile with a river; a thin line beside a field glows and the word furrow appears; fields fill with green; five colour swatches flip past; windmills pop up across a dry map; a dam wall is stamped constructed.
pacing: Slow reveal of the furrow, rapid colour code, three fast clue sets, firm close on the dam.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master the key, sort natural from constructed and read land use from symbols.
